clue.text: Boomerang champion let go

blocks.note: to back someone is to champion them
to fire an employee is to let them go

explanation.surface: A boomerang-throwing champion is released from a team or job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boomerang' is a verb here: a plan that boomerangs rebounds on its maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe a scheme that rebounds with bad results for the person who started it.

clue.text: Primate — shaggy hair own creation?

blocks.note: a bush of hair is a thick shaggy mass
a pet project is called someone's baby, their own creation

explanation.surface: A shaggy-haired monkey seems to be someone's pet creation.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushbaby, or galago, is a small big-eyed African primate, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Prowler perhaps catching male shark

indicators.note: a cat catching something holds it within its grasp

blocks.note: a cat is a typical prowler
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A prowling predator catches a male shark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shark' looks like the fish but means a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A shark is slang for a con artist or swindler, someone who cheats people.

clue.text: A mess, newspaper in Algarve city

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: Faro is the chief city of the Algarve in southern Portugal
rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid reports some disorder in a Portuguese resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble of things, a muddled mess.

clue.text: Some track bird

blocks.note: first meaning: one of the steel bars of a railway track
second meaning: a marsh bird such as the water ...

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher follows a trail left by a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is part of a railway line and also the name of a family of wading birds.

clue.text: Nation of Britain in recession, hang on!

indicators.note: something in recession goes backwards, so the abbreviation is read from right to left

blocks.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for Britain
'hang on!' means wait

explanation.surface: An economic news line: Britain in recession, so everyone holds tight.
explanation.definitionFit: Kuwait is a sovereign Gulf state, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Implement: hollowed-out tool in use when cooking

indicators.note: hollowing out a word scoops away its inside, keeping only its outer shell
cooking mixes ingredients up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: only the first and last letters of the word are kept
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kitchen tool so worn that it is hollow, still in use when cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement, especially one used in the kitchen.

clue.text: New approach penning conclusion of story, text often excluded

indicators.note: a new version of something is remade, so its letters are rearranged
penning something shuts it in a pen, so one part is enclosed by the other
the conclusion of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fresh approach to a story's ending leaves some text out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are biblical books excluded from many canons of scripture, so they are often left out.

clue.text: Attempt to net goal with it

indicators.note: netting something catches it inside, so one part goes around the other

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A footballer tries to put the ball in the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with it is fashionable and up to date, which is what trendy means.

clue.text: Odd pieces cut out, spam retains remarkably fresh flavour

indicators.note: odd pieces are stray leftovers, and cutting them out removes the spare letters from the fodder
something done remarkably is done in an unusual way, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook trims bits off some spam and finds it surprisingly fresh-tasting.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAM RETAINS has two letters too many; the stray A and S are the odd pieces cut out, and the other nine letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a mint plant used to give a cool, fresh taste to gum and sweets.

clue.text: In ancient city, last bits in pension fund suffering when going under?

indicators.note: one part sitting in another is enclosed by it
the last bits of words are their final letters

blocks.note: Thebes was a city of ancient Greece and also of ancient Egypt
the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: Pensioners in an old city suffer when their fund goes bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going under' hints at business failure but means diving underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: The bends is decompression sickness, the pain divers suffer after surfacing too fast from deep water.

clue.text: Saved by superhero, delegates go to pieces!

indicators.note: what is saved by the words is held safely inside them, spanning the gap between two of them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A superhero rescues a conference whose delegates are falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, crumbling bit by bit.

clue.text: Take a chance with fish shop

blocks.note: to bet is to take a chance
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Someone gambles by opening a fish shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' looks like a noun but is the slang verb: to shop someone is to inform on them to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to give someone away to the authorities or an enemy, a disloyal act of informing.

clue.text: Certain to get into drink — it's deliberate

indicators.note: one word getting into another ends up lodged inside it

blocks.note: mead is a drink made from honey
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone sure of themselves takes to drink on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Measured and deliberate both describe speech or action that is slow, careful and considered.

clue.text: Surrealist into an amazing mix of chemicals

indicators.note: one part going into another ends up inside it

blocks.note: 'some' expresses amazement, as in 'that was some party'
Salvador Dalí was the famous Surrealist painter

explanation.surface: A surrealist painter gets into an amazing mixture of chemicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda lime is a mixture of sodium hydroxide and calcium oxide, used to absorb carbon dioxide.

clue.text: Fool, regarding single mistake, shut up

blocks.note: the butt of a joke is the one made a fool of
on means about or regarding
one means single
a slip is a small mistake

explanation.surface: A fool, told off over one blunder, keeps quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stay silent, keeping one's mouth closed as if fastened.

clue.text: Pained grunt, boil causing distress

indicators.note: something pained is hurt and twisted, so these letters are contorted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a painful boil grunts in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Something troubling worries or upsets people, so it causes distress.

clue.text: Some wood, a hundred drifters at sea

blocks.note: a plank is a piece of wood
a ton is slang for a hundred

explanation.surface: Castaways adrift at sea cling to a piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are tiny organisms that drift with ocean currents rather than swimming.

clue.text: Finally, how might an inclusively unique show be performed?

definitions.text: how might an inclusively unique show be performed?

blocks.note: first meaning: conclusively, for good

blocks.clueFragment: how might an inclusively unique show be performed?
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: a unique show is put on a single time, and an inclusive one is open to everybody

explanation.surface: A theatre producer wonders how to stage a one-off show open to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: 'unique' supplies the first word of the phrase and 'inclusively' the last two.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means decisively and permanently, settling something so it never needs repeating.

clue.text: Report of defeats in game with strikers

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: to conquer is to defeat

explanation.surface: A sports report about defeats in a game with strikers.
explanation.walkthrough: Conkers is a British children's game: horse chestnuts on strings are swung to strike and break the opponent's nut.
explanation.definitionFit: In conkers each player strikes the other's chestnut with their own, so the nuts are the strikers.

clue.text: Play the fool ultimately in middle of monologue

indicators.note: ultimately points to what comes at the very end, the final letter
the middle of a word is its central few letters
one part placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the word
the three central letters of the nine

explanation.surface: An actor plays the fool at the climax of a monologue.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's tragedy, an example of a play.

clue.text: Cap discarded, steered a boat off

indicators.note: the cap is the top, and in a down answer that is the first letter, which is thrown away

blocks.note: one steers a canoe by paddling it

explanation.surface: Someone threw off their cap and paddled a boat away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' looks like an adverb of departure but describes food gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: An addled egg is rotten, so addled and off both mean gone bad.

clue.text: Stylish woman making first appearance, broadcasting

blocks.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman making her first appearance in society
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A stylish woman makes her TV debut.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a man who is suave, confident and elegantly dressed.

clue.text: Riser in the East rounding corner, Japanese ruler

indicators.note: something rounding another goes all the way around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: the sun rises in the east
to hog something is to corner it for yourself

explanation.surface: A rising figure in the Far East takes over before becoming a Japanese ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Japan is the Land of the Rising Sun, which helps the surface hide that 'Riser' is just the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was the hereditary military dictator of feudal Japan, its effective ruler.

clue.text: Energy observed in beautiful sparkle

indicators.note: something observed in another is seen sitting inside it

blocks.note: glam, short for glamorous, means beautiful
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Vitality is visible in a beautiful sparkle.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a brief flash or shine of light, which is a sparkle.

clue.text: Go for a spin?

blocks.note: first meaning: a go
second meaning: a rotation

explanation.surface: An invitation to take a drive in the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn is both a player's opportunity in a game and a single rotation about an axis.

clue.text: French runner, one in legend

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: lore is the body of traditional tales and legend
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A French athlete who has become a legend.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'runner' in crosswords is often a river, since rivers run.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, and rivers are crossword runners.

clue.text: Exuberant testament written by endless online trolls?

indicators.note: a document written by someone has their name next to it, so one part follows the other
something endless has lost its final part, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: E as in e-mail is the prefix for electronic or online
internet trolls act as bullies
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A will written by online trolls sounds rather gleeful.
explanation.walkthrough: Online trolls are cyberbullies, or e-bullies; drop the last S and add the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullient describes someone bubbling over with cheerful energy and enthusiasm.

clue.text: Break down summary

blocks.note: first meaning: to process food in the stomach
second meaning: a compilation or condensed account

explanation.surface: An instruction to analyse a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for processing food in the body and a noun for a condensed compendium of information.

clue.text: Rare, one abroad on public land

blocks.note: un is French for one
a common is open land for public use

explanation.surface: A rare sight: a foreigner out on the village common.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncommon is seldom met with, which is what rare means.
